01 · What we found

Four things stood out.

We went through saltairpilates.com the way a first-time guest would. Here’s what we saw, with the receipts.

Finding 01

Your only offer is for one person and one class.

The $30 first class on your homepage takes a third off your price, and it gives someone planning a group event nothing. The signup form in your footer offers wellness inspiration and updates, so most visitors have no reason to join the list. One offer can fix both.

Finding 02

Your 5-Class Pack is where the money is.

A first class with 10% off is $40.50. A 5-Class Pack is $175, more than four times that. The best time to offer it is the few days after a first class, while it still feels good. An automatic follow-up can do that for every guest.

Finding 03

The form asks how many are coming. It collects one email.

Plan Your Experience asks for the date, group size, town and type of experience, plus one name and one email. A bachelorette brings the whole party to the mat, and the end of a great morning is the best time to invite every guest to join. Those same answers can also send a bachelorette and a hotel completely different follow-ups.

Finding 04

Your summer guests are your easiest next bookings.

Everyone who booked a class this summer gave you their email at checkout. They already know and like Salt Air, so they’re the easiest people to bring back. If they agreed to hear from you, keep them close until next summer. Tell them about the weekend class, holiday gifts and first pick of summer dates.

02 · The point

The first class sells itself. The second one needs a reason.a nudge.a Friday text.an invite.a 5-Class Pack.a reason.

Email and text give people that reason. New people get 10% off their first booking. First-timers get a pack offer while the class still feels good. Every guest at a private event gets an invite, and past guests get first pick of summer dates.

We bring the studio to you.

03 · The plan

Six flows, each one aimed at a finding

Flows are emails and texts that send themselves when a guest does something. Once they’re live, they work every day without anyone pressing send.

Who does what

The simple rule is that anything in an inbox, a text thread or a signup form is ours. The mat is yours.

Paid ads, social media, photography and new site pages sit outside this retainer. Klaviyo and text sending fees are billed to Salt Air directly.

03 · The plan, in practice

What a guest actually sees

A link the organizer shares with the group, a holiday email and texts that sound like you. These are examples.

Example texts

Right after signup

Salt Air: Welcome! Here’s 10% off your first booking, whether it’s a class for you or a private experience for your crew. It applies automatically at saltairpilates.com. Reply STOP to opt out.

Friday, 5:00 PM

Salt Air: Mats are out tomorrow at 10 at Topping Rose House. All levels welcome. Save your spot at saltairpilates.com

Night before an event

Salt Air: Rain is in tomorrow’s forecast, so your group’s session is moving under cover. Same time, same crew. See you there 🩵

05 · The first 90 days

Built in the off-season, ready for summer

We can kick off within a week of approval. The signup offer and holiday gift guide go live before Black Friday.

  1. 1

    Weeks 1 and 2 · Early November

    Set up

    • Kickoff call, plus access to Shopify and Klaviyo. Not on Klaviyo yet? We set it up.

  2. 2

    Month 1 · November

    First flows live

  3. 3
